monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp, intentional reduction in volume and intensity compared to last month’s peak training — likely reflective of planned recovery or fatigue management.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence jumped +27 spm this month (145 vs 118) — the largest single-month improvement in the dataset, aligning with reduced pace and lower HR, suggesting conscious effort toward relaxed, economical turnover.

goal_tracker.message: Matching last month’s 82.4 km would require 76.4 km across 12 sessions in 27 days — an unsustainable ~2.8 km/session average, especially given chronic sleep debt (14/14 nights <7h) and low training readiness (25/100). Chasing this number is inadvisable; recovery consolidation must precede volume rebound.

insights.title: Chronic sleep restriction correlates with elevated aerobic decoupling
insights.body: Despite improved HRV and resting HR, aerobic decoupling median is 7.11% (well above 5% threshold), and 14/14 nights had <7h sleep — suggesting insufficient sleep impairs metabolic efficiency during longer efforts.

insights.title: ACWR is optimal (1.0) but masks underlying fatigue
insights.body: ACWR sits at 1.0 (acute 251, chronic 230), yet training readiness is only 25 and recovery balance (+2.7) is driven by acute load collapse (last week’s TRIMP dropped to 170 from 625), not improved recovery capacity.

insights.title: Cadence surge coincides with improved efficiency and lower aerobic TE
insights.body: Cadence rose +27 spm (118 → 145) while efficiency improved (-0.07 ml/kg/km) and aerobic TE dropped (-0.8), indicating better neuromuscular coordination and reduced energy cost per stride — likely aided by recent very easy runs (e.g., 20+ min/km efforts on 2026-07-31).

insights.title: VO2max increased +2.5 vs baseline despite low-volume month
insights.body: VO2max rose to 39.6 (from baseline 36.7), +6.7%, even as monthly volume collapsed — confirming that quality (e.g., 14.8 km long run at 9:07/km in July) and recovery-sensitive adaptations can progress without high volume when sleep and HRV are managed well — though current sleep debt threatens sustainability.

recommendations.reason: Maintains aerobic stimulus without taxing recovery systems; aligns with current readiness score (25) and improved Zone 2 efficiency (0.7879 m/beat)
